Let \([S]\) denote area. Use the standard lemma:

**Lemma.** If a parallelogram \(P\) is contained in a triangle \(T\), then
\[
[P]\le \frac12 [T].
\]

*Proof sketch.* By affine invariance, take \(T=\Delta=\{(x,y):x\ge0,\ y\ge0,\ x+y\le1\}\), so \([\Delta]=\frac12\). Let \(P\) have center \(c\) and half-edge vectors \(u,v\), written in barycentric coordinates. Since all vertices \(c\pm u\pm v\) lie in \(\Delta\),
\[
|u_i|+|v_i|\le c_i \quad (i=1,2,3).
\]
Summing gives
\[
A+B\le 1,\qquad A=\sum |u_i|,\ B=\sum |v_i|.
\]
For zero-sum plane vectors, \(|u\times v|\le AB/4\). Hence
\[
[P]=4|u\times v|\le AB\le \frac{(A+B)^2}{4}\le \frac14=\frac12[\Delta].
\]
So the lemma holds.

A unit square is a parallelogram of area \(1\). Therefore any triangle containing it has area at least
\[
2\cdot 1=2.
\]
This bound is attained by the triangle with vertices \((-1,0),(1,0),(0,2)\), which contains the unit square \([-\frac12,\frac12]\times[0,1]\) and has area
\[
\frac12\cdot 2\cdot 2=2.
\]

Thus the minimum area is
\[
\boxed{2}.
\]
